1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE 50% : The buyer can increase or decrease the contract quantity or contract duration up to 50 percent at the time of issue of the contract. However, once the contract is issued, the contract quantity or contract duration can only be increased up to 50 percent. Bidders are bound to accept the revised quantity or duration. For lumpsum-based service contracts, the buyer may increase the scope of work and contract value up to 50 percent with the consent of the service provider 2. Certificates Bidder's offer is liable to be rejected if they don't upload any of the certificates / documents sought in the Bid document, ATC and Corrigendum if any. 3. Service & Support AVAILABILITY OF OFFICE OF SERVICE PROVIDER: An office of the Service Provider must be located in the state of Consignee. DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE TO BE SUBMITTED. 4. Service & Support Dedicated /toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support : BIDDER/OEM must have Dedicated/toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support. 5. Service & Support Escalation Matrix For Service Support : Bidder/OEM must provide Escalation Matrix of Telephone Numbers for Service Support. 6. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses 1. Mandatory Pre-Bid Site Inspection & Deemed Acceptance · Site Inspection: Bidders must physically inspect all 63 air conditioning units, including indoor evaporator units, outdoor condensing units, compressors, copper refrigerant piping, condensate drain lines, electronic control boards (PCBs), electrical isolators/MCBs, and mounting brackets across all designated premises (M ain Building: Ground to 3rd Floor, and Guest House) before submitting their bid. Special attention must be paid to outdoor units installed at heights on external building walls and ledges. · Binding Quotes: Submission of the bid confirms that the bidder has verified the physical and operational c ondition of every machine. All units will be handed over on an "as-is, where-is" basis. No claims for extra charges, unforeseen repairs, obsolete spare sourcing, or price escalation on grounds of pre-existing machi ne condition, height access, or vintage will be entertained after bid award. · Inspection Certificate: Bidders must obtain and upload a Site Visit Certificate duly signed by the authorize d buyer representative along with their technical bid. Bids submitted without site inspection proof are liabl e for rejection. 2. Annual Preventive Maintenance & Servicing Structure The contractor must execute a structured 3-stage maintenance program for every unit during the one- year contract period, comprising One Preventive Maintenance (Overhaul) + One Routine Wet Servi ce + One Routine Dry Service, in addition to attending to unlimited breakdown calls: · Stage 1: Preventive Maintenance & Comprehensive Overhaul (Commencement ) o Must be initiated immediately and completed within fifteen (15) days of contract commence ment. o Complete operational audit and diagnostic testing of all 63 units. o Rectification, overhaul, or replacement of defective/weak compressors, condenser coils, eva porator coils, blower fan motors, outdoor condenser motors, PCBs, capacitors, contactors,

expansion valves, and associated control wiring. o Pressure-testing with dry nitrogen, vacuum evacuation, and full refrigerant charging (R-32, R-410A, or R-22) for any units with gas leakage or low cooling performance. o Deep cleaning, motor lubrication, electrical terminal retightening, and mounting bracket sta bility inspection. · Stage 2: Routine Wet Servicing (Mid-Term ) o One mandatory mid-cycle deep wet-cleaning using high-pressure jet wash machines and ch emical coil cleaners. o High-pressure jet cleaning of outdoor condenser coils to remove dirt, grease, and debris. o Jet washing of indoor cooling coils, blower wheel assemblies, and air filters. o Flushing, sanitizing, and clearing of condensate drain trays and drain piping to eliminate blo ckages and mold buildup. · Stage 3: Routine Dry Servicing & Performance Audit o One comprehensive dry service, filter dusting, and mechanical inspection before seasonal t emperature shifts. o Electrical check: measuring operating current draw (amperes), voltage, earth continuity, an d tightness of all electrical lugs/isolators. o Refrigerant circuit check: testing suction/discharge pressures, checking flare nut joints for oi l traces/leaks, and recording cooling delta temperature. o Blower balancing, fan blade alignment, noise/vibration checks, and thermostat/sensor calibr ation. 3. Breakdown Maintenance & Service Turnaround (SLA) · Complaint Logging: Breakdown calls will be logged via email, phone, or messaging to the contractor's d esignated contact. · Response Time: A qualified HVAC technician must report on-site within four (4) hours of complaint noti fication. · Rectification Turnaround: o Minor Faults (capacitors, sensors, remotes, gas top-ups, drain choke, minor wiring): Rectifie d within twenty-four (24) hours. o Major Faults (compressor replacement, coil replacement, PCB repair/replacement, motor fail ure): Rectified within forty-eight (48) hours. · 4. Comprehensive Scope of Spares & Consumables · The contract is 100% Comprehensive. The contractor must supply and replace all defective spares free of cost throughout the contract period. · Included Components: Hermetic/rotary/inverter compressors, condenser coils (copper), evaporator coils ( copper), condenser fan motors, indoor blower motors, PCB main boards, inverter control modules, display boards, temperature/room sensors, capacitors, contactors, relays, expansion valves, 3-pin power plugs, is olator switches, remotes, and refrigerant gas charging (including evacuation, vacuuming, and leak testing) . 5. Safety Standards for Working at Heights & Statutory Liabilities · Outdoor condensing units located across the First, Second, and Third Floors are mounted on external wall s, window ledges, and cantilever brackets. The service provider must ensure their technicians use standar d Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including full-body safety harnesses with lifelines, safety helmets, non-slip footwear, and certified ladders/scaffolding. · The service provider bears sole legal and financial responsibility for statutory compliance with the Contrac

t Labour (R&A) Act, Minimum Wages Act, Workmen Compensation Act, EPF, and ESIC regulations. The buye r accepts no liability for accidental injury, fall, or fatality occurring during maintenance operations. 6. Contract Documentation, Invoicing & Hand back · Initial Joint Condition Report: A joint inspection report recording baseline operating parameters, serial numbers, and physical condition of all 63 units must be signed within seven (7) days of contract commenc ement. · Contract Expiry Handback: Upon completion of the AMC period, the service provider must hand back al l 63 air conditioners in fully operational, gas-charged, and clean working condition. The final payment will b e released only after a joint verification clearance certificate is issued by the buyer. .
